I actually have synesthesia (and I'm blessed with the misophonia that most synesthetes have too, yay). It's often misunderstood as living this trippy life where you see sounds, taste colours, etc. However it's actually much more subtle, more like a mental association thing.

My own personal synesthesia manifests itself as a really intense reaction to the "feel" of a place. It's hard to explain, but some places trigger music, music can also trigger memories of places or evoke the same "feel" of a place, other places trigger overwhelming emotions of different types that make being in the place an intense experience. Some places feel bad, so bad that sometimes they make me feel physically nauseous and I have to leave. Weird things like utility poles and pylons make me feel better about a place. As a result I have some unusual ways of enjoying places, and my memories of the past are mostly coloured by the "atmosphere" and vibe that I felt at the time from the place I was in. Some places have a strange and weird vibe to them that makes me curious, causing me to keep returning.

As a result, from a pretty early age I became an urban explorer, and I have a hard drive full of folders of photos I took at abandoned places that I've explored. Many of my strongest memories and favourite pieces of music are associated with these places.

The weather also has it's own effect. I remember when I was a kid, looking out the window at the overcast sky, and telling my dad that it was "an exploring day". He was really confused as to how I'd come to the conclusion that today was a day we should get in the car and go find things to explore, so I explained that it was cloudy, and cloudy days are just exploring days.

Also when I think about days of the week, in my head it looks like a bar chart. Monday is the lowest day on the graph, and sunday is the highest day. There are probably a ton of other things like this that I do without noticing it.

I have no interest in taking acid. My life (and music) is funky enough without it.

I think you're possibly misunderstanding my post as attempting to characterise my synesthesia as being standard. Perhaps I didn't emphasise strongly enough that this is my own personal synesthesia - others are different. But that doesn't change the fact that the common "living life in an acid trip" myth is simply incorrect. I don't like being compared to drug users, or having anyone imply that I'm mentally impaired or sensually overloaded. I'm as normal as the next person, I just have a kind of funky experience of the world.

Also, it's not something that I've positively incorporated into my life as such, it's just something that I was born with and thought was normal until I found out that it wasn't. While it has it's perks, and I value the rare opportunity to experience life in such a unique way, it does have it's downsides.

It actually makes me fearful/anxious of completely new places that I've never seen before in case I end up somewhere that makes me feel sick. This fear makes me want to seek to repeat pleasant familiarity rather than risk unpleasant newness. London (UK) for instance is a city that makes me feel sick, and each time I go there I have to force myself to ignore the bad bits and make a bee line for the nice bits (Hyde Park, Richmond, etc.) so that I can enjoy the amazing culture and buzz that London has to offer rather than living a sheltered life.

Another example would be when I suffered a lot of anxiety when I was emigrating to Canada, and had to comfort myself by going on google streetview to make sure that it wasn't actually going to feel bad. Turns out this place looks just like it does in the movies, which was the North America that I'd always pictured in my head, and was everything I'd hoped it'd be. But the lingering doubt might've stopped me from moving if I hadn't controlled it.

The upshot of this is that I've felt good vibes from pictures of places on the internet, which has encouraged me to investigate further and put those locations on my travel wishlist. So those are places I feel good about traveling to and I can get excited about them. It's not all bad news.
